 Our Animals 
 
 118 species, 22 critically endangered species. 
 
 The inhabitants of the Alabama Gulf Coast Zoo are a richly diverse and decidedly unique population for a small-town community zoo. Every single animal has a name and a backstory. No matter their beginnings or their circumstances, they all have a loving and safe home at Alabama Gulf Coast Zoo. Meet our animals!

#SupportYourLocalZoo #AnimalsandArt #AGCZArtontheWildSideRead moreAlabama Gulf Coast ZooMarch 14, 2026ViewRed Wolf Update: A Big Step for Jenkins
If you’ve been following the journey of our two new red wolves, Jenkins and Walker, we have a wonderful milestone to share. Jenkins has been spotted exploring the yard of his habitat during the day.
This is an exciting sign that he’s becoming more comfortable in his surroundings and beginning to confidently investigate his new environment. For a species that is naturally shy and cautious, especially in human care, this kind of daytime exploration is a meaningful step forward. 

Want to learn more about these critically endangered wolves? Come visit the Zoo and see conservation in action.

 DYK?
Red wolves are one of the most critically endangered canids in the world.
A few key facts:
* Fewer than 20 red wolves remain in the wild today, all in eastern North Carolina.
* A little over 200 red wolves live under human care in zoos and wildlife centers.
* The SAFE (Saving Animals From Extinction) American Red Wolf Program works to research, breed, and prepare these wolves for potential release back into the wild.
* Protecting red wolves helps protect entire ecosystems by keeping populations of deer, raccoons, and rodents in balance.Read more21/5Alabama Gulf Coast ZooMarch 14, 2026ViewWe’re out and about at the BB-Q & Blues Cook Off in Downtown Foley!

Come on out and see us — we’ve brought some of our favorite Animal Ambassadors along for the fun!

Say hello to Rose the opossum, Lucy the three‑banded armadillo, Mia the Central American boa, and Mailbox the box turtle. They’re soaking up the sunshine, the music, and all the friendly faces.

If you’re wandering the festival today, swing by and visit. We’d love to see you!

review.reviewBody: Nice
Gulf Shores hidden gem.

Really fun time with the family here. Clean inside the buildings and the staff was nice to us. We had a group of 12 😅  Do you guys have a link for purchasing merchandise online? My son retrospectively would like a T-shirt but we&#039;re back home now in TX lol

Kids fed the giraffe! Honestly the only disappointing thing was the cost of the stuffed animals. $25 a piece? I would&#039;ve gotten em but I&#039;m not spending $100 (4 kiddos) on a regular stuffed animal.

I really want half my money back.  Nothing was really open .  Almost all the animals was gone or inside .  No food bar , the best thing was feeding the animals.  This was a waste of time and really doesn’t deserve a rating.  If you are not going to be able to give what you advertise please stop .  Thank you
A bit on the small side for the cost of admission. Imo BUT has lots of small monkeys monkeys and all the cats Displays are well laid out as we could see all the critters
The animals were well cared for. It was a very pretty zoo with lots of very neat animals.

What staff we came across were friendly, most animals were lazy, &amp; didn&#039;t move around, it was a warm day, but still?? Anything extra like walking in the lemuer enclosure was x-tra ( $25 )  prices were way high, not worth the price. So underwhelmed with my experience.
Okay,  very nice,  clean and friendly.  Nice paths to stroll. Could have more benches and more animals. Sad to say but needs more animals.

Perfect size zoo, you can see every exhibit in a morning or afternoon. Great variety of monkeys and cats. But they have a surprising amount of other animals. You can buy tickets to feed the giraffes too.
The worst zoo we went there 6 moths ago and the cashier was just horribly disrespectful. The zoo is too expensive the enclosures were dirty.

 Tickets are now on sale for Art on the Wild Side: Wine & Whiskey Stroll, the annual spring fundraiser benefiting your local nonprofit Alabama Gulf Coast Zoo.Guests (21+) are invited to enjoy an unforgettable evening on Saturday, March 28, 2026, strolling through the zoo while sampling fine wines, craft whiskeys, and gourmet bites surrounded by your favorite animal ambassadors. Guests will have the opportunity to meet animal ambassadors and experience animal training demonstrations.Art on the Wild Side begins with an online auction on March 21, which includes one-of-a-kind, unique pieces of art created by the zoo animals. Whether painted with paws, claws, fur, footprints, or nose boops, each piece is a true masterpiece. The auction also includes vacation packages, golf outings, and more, generously donated by local businesses and community members.As a local non-profit organization, the support from this event is critical to helping provide care and enrichment to the animals that call the zoo home. This includes fresh diets, healthcare, habitats that include climbing structures, perching, ropes, and more that keep each animal from the smallest hedgehog to the largest lion healthy, active and mentally engaged.Your support also helps the zoo provide hands-on conservation education and programs throughout the community that continue the Zoo’s mission of connecting people of all ages with wildlife and encouraging them to protect the world around them.Tickets to the annual fundraiser are $125 per person, and $100 per person for Zoo Members. Sponsorship packages are available and include varying levels of benefits. Click here to purchase tickets and for more information.Special thanks to Visionary Sponsors Dr. Mike and Janet Asher and the City of Orange Beach.###

#SupportYourLocalZoo #AnimalsandArt #AGCZArtontheWildSideRead moreAlabama Gulf Coast ZooMarch 14, 2026ViewRed Wolf Update: A Big Step for Jenkins
If you’ve been following the journey of our two new red wolves, Jenkins and Walker, we have a wonderful milestone to share. Jenkins has been spotted exploring the yard of his habitat during the day.
This is an exciting sign that he’s becoming more comfortable in his surroundings and beginning to confidently investigate his new environment. For a species that is naturally shy and cautious, especially in human care, this kind of daytime exploration is a meaningful step forward. 

Want to learn more about these critically endangered wolves? Come visit the Zoo and see conservation in action.

 DYK?
Red wolves are one of the most critically endangered canids in the world.
A few key facts:
* Fewer than 20 red wolves remain in the wild today, all in eastern North Carolina.
* A little over 200 red wolves live under human care in zoos and wildlife centers.
* The SAFE (Saving Animals From Extinction) American Red Wolf Program works to research, breed, and prepare these wolves for potential release back into the wild.
* Protecting red wolves helps protect entire ecosystems by keeping populations of deer, raccoons, and rodents in balance.Read more21/5Alabama Gulf Coast ZooMarch 14, 2026ViewWe’re out and about at the BB-Q & Blues Cook Off in Downtown Foley!

Come on out and see us — we’ve brought some of our favorite Animal Ambassadors along for the fun!

Say hello to Rose the opossum, Lucy the three‑banded armadillo, Mia the Central American boa, and Mailbox the box turtle. They’re soaking up the sunshine, the music, and all the friendly faces.

If you’re wandering the festival today, swing by and visit. We’d love to see you!

review.reviewBody: Nice
Gulf Shores hidden gem.

Really fun time with the family here. Clean inside the buildings and the staff was nice to us. We had a group of 12 😅  Do you guys have a link for purchasing merchandise online? My son retrospectively would like a T-shirt but we&#039;re back home now in TX lol

Kids fed the giraffe! Honestly the only disappointing thing was the cost of the stuffed animals. $25 a piece? I would&#039;ve gotten em but I&#039;m not spending $100 (4 kiddos) on a regular stuffed animal.

I really want half my money back.  Nothing was really open .  Almost all the animals was gone or inside .  No food bar , the best thing was feeding the animals.  This was a waste of time and really doesn’t deserve a rating.  If you are not going to be able to give what you advertise please stop .  Thank you
A bit on the small side for the cost of admission. Imo BUT has lots of small monkeys monkeys and all the cats Displays are well laid out as we could see all the critters
The animals were well cared for. It was a very pretty zoo with lots of very neat animals.

What staff we came across were friendly, most animals were lazy, &amp; didn&#039;t move around, it was a warm day, but still?? Anything extra like walking in the lemuer enclosure was x-tra ( $25 )  prices were way high, not worth the price. So underwhelmed with my experience.
Okay,  very nice,  clean and friendly.  Nice paths to stroll. Could have more benches and more animals. Sad to say but needs more animals.

Perfect size zoo, you can see every exhibit in a morning or afternoon. Great variety of monkeys and cats. But they have a surprising amount of other animals. You can buy tickets to feed the giraffes too.
The worst zoo we went there 6 moths ago and the cashier was just horribly disrespectful. The zoo is too expensive the enclosures were dirty.

Contact Barn Chat: 2:15 pm – 2:45 pm. Meet at the Contact Barn.
Experience the joy of animal interaction at the “Contact Barn Chat” at the Alabama Gulf Coast Zoo! This engaging session allows visitors to get up close and personal with some of our friendly barnyard animals. Join our knowledgeable keepers as they introduce you to our charming goats, sheep, chickens, and more. Learn about their care, feeding habits, and the important roles they play in agriculture and everyday life. You’ll have the chance to pet and feed these gentle animals while gaining insights into their unique personalities and behaviors. The “Contact Barn Chat” is a perfect activity for families and animal lovers, offering a hands-on, educational adventure that you won’t forget!

review.reviewBody: Nice
Gulf Shores hidden gem.

Really fun time with the family here. Clean inside the buildings and the staff was nice to us. We had a group of 12 😅  Do you guys have a link for purchasing merchandise online? My son retrospectively would like a T-shirt but we&#039;re back home now in TX lol

Kids fed the giraffe! Honestly the only disappointing thing was the cost of the stuffed animals. $25 a piece? I would&#039;ve gotten em but I&#039;m not spending $100 (4 kiddos) on a regular stuffed animal.

I really want half my money back.  Nothing was really open .  Almost all the animals was gone or inside .  No food bar , the best thing was feeding the animals.  This was a waste of time and really doesn’t deserve a rating.  If you are not going to be able to give what you advertise please stop .  Thank you
A bit on the small side for the cost of admission. Imo BUT has lots of small monkeys monkeys and all the cats Displays are well laid out as we could see all the critters
The animals were well cared for. It was a very pretty zoo with lots of very neat animals.

What staff we came across were friendly, most animals were lazy, &amp; didn&#039;t move around, it was a warm day, but still?? Anything extra like walking in the lemuer enclosure was x-tra ( $25 )  prices were way high, not worth the price. So underwhelmed with my experience.
Okay,  very nice,  clean and friendly.  Nice paths to stroll. Could have more benches and more animals. Sad to say but needs more animals.

Perfect size zoo, you can see every exhibit in a morning or afternoon. Great variety of monkeys and cats. But they have a surprising amount of other animals. You can buy tickets to feed the giraffes too.
The worst zoo we went there 6 moths ago and the cashier was just horribly disrespectful. The zoo is too expensive the enclosures were dirty.

Contact Barn Chat: 2:15 pm – 2:45 pm. Meet at the Contact Barn.
Experience the joy of animal interaction at the “Contact Barn Chat” at the Alabama Gulf Coast Zoo! This engaging session allows visitors to get up close and personal with some of our friendly barnyard animals. Join our knowledgeable keepers as they introduce you to our charming goats, sheep, chickens, and more. Learn about their care, feeding habits, and the important roles they play in agriculture and everyday life. You’ll have the chance to pet and feed these gentle animals while gaining insights into their unique personalities and behaviors. The “Contact Barn Chat” is a perfect activity for families and animal lovers, offering a hands-on, educational adventure that you won’t forget!

#SupportYourLocalZoo #AnimalsandArt #AGCZArtontheWildSideRead moreAlabama Gulf Coast ZooMarch 14, 2026ViewRed Wolf Update: A Big Step for Jenkins
If you’ve been following the journey of our two new red wolves, Jenkins and Walker, we have a wonderful milestone to share. Jenkins has been spotted exploring the yard of his habitat during the day.
This is an exciting sign that he’s becoming more comfortable in his surroundings and beginning to confidently investigate his new environment. For a species that is naturally shy and cautious, especially in human care, this kind of daytime exploration is a meaningful step forward. 

Want to learn more about these critically endangered wolves? Come visit the Zoo and see conservation in action.

 DYK?
Red wolves are one of the most critically endangered canids in the world.
A few key facts:
* Fewer than 20 red wolves remain in the wild today, all in eastern North Carolina.
* A little over 200 red wolves live under human care in zoos and wildlife centers.
* The SAFE (Saving Animals From Extinction) American Red Wolf Program works to research, breed, and prepare these wolves for potential release back into the wild.
* Protecting red wolves helps protect entire ecosystems by keeping populations of deer, raccoons, and rodents in balance.Read more21/5Alabama Gulf Coast ZooMarch 14, 2026ViewWe’re out and about at the BB-Q & Blues Cook Off in Downtown Foley!

Come on out and see us — we’ve brought some of our favorite Animal Ambassadors along for the fun!

Say hello to Rose the opossum, Lucy the three‑banded armadillo, Mia the Central American boa, and Mailbox the box turtle. They’re soaking up the sunshine, the music, and all the friendly faces.

If you’re wandering the festival today, swing by and visit. We’d love to see you!

#SupportYourLocalZoo #AnimalsandArt #AGCZArtontheWildSideRead moreAlabama Gulf Coast ZooMarch 14, 2026ViewRed Wolf Update: A Big Step for Jenkins
If you’ve been following the journey of our two new red wolves, Jenkins and Walker, we have a wonderful milestone to share. Jenkins has been spotted exploring the yard of his habitat during the day.
This is an exciting sign that he’s becoming more comfortable in his surroundings and beginning to confidently investigate his new environment. For a species that is naturally shy and cautious, especially in human care, this kind of daytime exploration is a meaningful step forward. 

Want to learn more about these critically endangered wolves? Come visit the Zoo and see conservation in action.

 DYK?
Red wolves are one of the most critically endangered canids in the world.
A few key facts:
* Fewer than 20 red wolves remain in the wild today, all in eastern North Carolina.
* A little over 200 red wolves live under human care in zoos and wildlife centers.
* The SAFE (Saving Animals From Extinction) American Red Wolf Program works to research, breed, and prepare these wolves for potential release back into the wild.
* Protecting red wolves helps protect entire ecosystems by keeping populations of deer, raccoons, and rodents in balance.Read more21/5Alabama Gulf Coast ZooMarch 14, 2026ViewWe’re out and about at the BB-Q & Blues Cook Off in Downtown Foley!

Come on out and see us — we’ve brought some of our favorite Animal Ambassadors along for the fun!

Say hello to Rose the opossum, Lucy the three‑banded armadillo, Mia the Central American boa, and Mailbox the box turtle. They’re soaking up the sunshine, the music, and all the friendly faces.

If you’re wandering the festival today, swing by and visit. We’d love to see you!

review.reviewBody: Nice
Gulf Shores hidden gem.

Really fun time with the family here. Clean inside the buildings and the staff was nice to us. We had a group of 12 😅  Do you guys have a link for purchasing merchandise online? My son retrospectively would like a T-shirt but we&#039;re back home now in TX lol

Kids fed the giraffe! Honestly the only disappointing thing was the cost of the stuffed animals. $25 a piece? I would&#039;ve gotten em but I&#039;m not spending $100 (4 kiddos) on a regular stuffed animal.

I really want half my money back.  Nothing was really open .  Almost all the animals was gone or inside .  No food bar , the best thing was feeding the animals.  This was a waste of time and really doesn’t deserve a rating.  If you are not going to be able to give what you advertise please stop .  Thank you
A bit on the small side for the cost of admission. Imo BUT has lots of small monkeys monkeys and all the cats Displays are well laid out as we could see all the critters
The animals were well cared for. It was a very pretty zoo with lots of very neat animals.

What staff we came across were friendly, most animals were lazy, &amp; didn&#039;t move around, it was a warm day, but still?? Anything extra like walking in the lemuer enclosure was x-tra ( $25 )  prices were way high, not worth the price. So underwhelmed with my experience.
Okay,  very nice,  clean and friendly.  Nice paths to stroll. Could have more benches and more animals. Sad to say but needs more animals.

Perfect size zoo, you can see every exhibit in a morning or afternoon. Great variety of monkeys and cats. But they have a surprising amount of other animals. You can buy tickets to feed the giraffes too.
The worst zoo we went there 6 moths ago and the cashier was just horribly disrespectful. The zoo is too expensive the enclosures were dirty.

Contact Barn Chat: 2:15 pm – 2:45 pm. Meet at the Contact Barn.
Experience the joy of animal interaction at the “Contact Barn Chat” at the Alabama Gulf Coast Zoo! This engaging session allows visitors to get up close and personal with some of our friendly barnyard animals. Join our knowledgeable keepers as they introduce you to our charming goats, sheep, chickens, and more. Learn about their care, feeding habits, and the important roles they play in agriculture and everyday life. You’ll have the chance to pet and feed these gentle animals while gaining insights into their unique personalities and behaviors. The “Contact Barn Chat” is a perfect activity for families and animal lovers, offering a hands-on, educational adventure that you won’t forget!

Contact Barn Chat: 2:15 pm – 2:45 pm. Meet at the Contact Barn.
Experience the joy of animal interaction at the “Contact Barn Chat” at the Alabama Gulf Coast Zoo! This engaging session allows visitors to get up close and personal with some of our friendly barnyard animals. Join our knowledgeable keepers as they introduce you to our charming goats, sheep, chickens, and more. Learn about their care, feeding habits, and the important roles they play in agriculture and everyday life. You’ll have the chance to pet and feed these gentle animals while gaining insights into their unique personalities and behaviors. The “Contact Barn Chat” is a perfect activity for families and animal lovers, offering a hands-on, educational adventure that you won’t forget!

If you’ve been following the journey of our two new red wolves, Jenkins and Walker, we have a wonderful milestone to share. Jenkins has been spotted exploring the yard of his habitat during the day.
This is an exciting sign that he’s becoming more comfortable in his surroundings and beginning to confidently investigate his new environment. For a species that is naturally shy and cautious, especially in human care, this kind of daytime exploration is a meaningful step forward. 

Want to learn more about these critically endangered wolves? Come visit the Zoo and see conservation in action.

 DYK?
Red wolves are one of the most critically endangered canids in the world.

* Fewer than 20 red wolves remain in the wild today, all in eastern North Carolina.

If you’ve been following the journey of our two new red wolves, Jenkins and Walker, we have a wonderful milestone to share. Jenkins has been spotted exploring the yard of his habitat during the day.
This is an exciting sign that he’s becoming more comfortable in his surroundings and beginning to confidently investigate his new environment. For a species that is naturally shy and cautious, especially in human care, this kind of daytime exploration is a meaningful step forward. 

Want to learn more about these critically endangered wolves? Come visit the Zoo and see conservation in action.

 DYK?
Red wolves are one of the most critically endangered canids in the world.
A few key facts:
* Fewer than 20 red wolves remain in the wild today, all in eastern North Carolina.
* A little over 200 red wolves live under human care in zoos and wildlife centers.
* The SAFE (Saving Animals From Extinction) American Red Wolf Program works to research, breed, and prepare these wolves for potential release back into the wild.
* Protecting red wolves helps protect entire ecosystems by keeping populations of deer, raccoons, and rodents in balance.Read more21/5Alabama Gulf Coast ZooMarch 14, 2026ViewWe’re out and about at the BB-Q & Blues Cook Off in Downtown Foley!

Come on out and see us — we’ve brought some of our favorite Animal Ambassadors along for the fun!

Say hello to Rose the opossum, Lucy the three‑banded armadillo, Mia the Central American boa, and Mailbox the box turtle. They’re soaking up the sunshine, the music, and all the friendly faces.

If you’re wandering the festival today, swing by and visit. We’d love to see you!

review.reviewBody: Nice
Gulf Shores hidden gem.

Really fun time with the family here. Clean inside the buildings and the staff was nice to us. We had a group of 12 😅  Do you guys have a link for purchasing merchandise online? My son retrospectively would like a T-shirt but we&#039;re back home now in TX lol

Kids fed the giraffe! Honestly the only disappointing thing was the cost of the stuffed animals. $25 a piece? I would&#039;ve gotten em but I&#039;m not spending $100 (4 kiddos) on a regular stuffed animal.

I really want half my money back.  Nothing was really open .  Almost all the animals was gone or inside .  No food bar , the best thing was feeding the animals.  This was a waste of time and really doesn’t deserve a rating.  If you are not going to be able to give what you advertise please stop .  Thank you
A bit on the small side for the cost of admission. Imo BUT has lots of small monkeys monkeys and all the cats Displays are well laid out as we could see all the critters
The animals were well cared for. It was a very pretty zoo with lots of very neat animals.

What staff we came across were friendly, most animals were lazy, &amp; didn&#039;t move around, it was a warm day, but still?? Anything extra like walking in the lemuer enclosure was x-tra ( $25 )  prices were way high, not worth the price. So underwhelmed with my experience.
Okay,  very nice,  clean and friendly.  Nice paths to stroll. Could have more benches and more animals. Sad to say but needs more animals.

Perfect size zoo, you can see every exhibit in a morning or afternoon. Great variety of monkeys and cats. But they have a surprising amount of other animals. You can buy tickets to feed the giraffes too.
The worst zoo we went there 6 moths ago and the cashier was just horribly disrespectful. The zoo is too expensive the enclosures were dirty.

review.reviewBody: Nice
Gulf Shores hidden gem.

Really fun time with the family here. Clean inside the buildings and the staff was nice to us. We had a group of 12 😅  Do you guys have a link for purchasing merchandise online? My son retrospectively would like a T-shirt but we&#039;re back home now in TX lol

Kids fed the giraffe! Honestly the only disappointing thing was the cost of the stuffed animals. $25 a piece? I would&#039;ve gotten em but I&#039;m not spending $100 (4 kiddos) on a regular stuffed animal.

I really want half my money back.  Nothing was really open .  Almost all the animals was gone or inside .  No food bar , the best thing was feeding the animals.  This was a waste of time and really doesn’t deserve a rating.  If you are not going to be able to give what you advertise please stop .  Thank you
A bit on the small side for the cost of admission. Imo BUT has lots of small monkeys monkeys and all the cats Displays are well laid out as we could see all the critters
The animals were well cared for. It was a very pretty zoo with lots of very neat animals.

What staff we came across were friendly, most animals were lazy, &amp; didn&#039;t move around, it was a warm day, but still?? Anything extra like walking in the lemuer enclosure was x-tra ( $25 )  prices were way high, not worth the price. So underwhelmed with my experience.
Okay,  very nice,  clean and friendly.  Nice paths to stroll. Could have more benches and more animals. Sad to say but needs more animals.

Perfect size zoo, you can see every exhibit in a morning or afternoon. Great variety of monkeys and cats. But they have a surprising amount of other animals. You can buy tickets to feed the giraffes too.
The worst zoo we went there 6 moths ago and the cashier was just horribly disrespectful. The zoo is too expensive the enclosures were dirty.

#SupportYourLocalZoo #AnimalsandArt #AGCZArtontheWildSideRead moreAlabama Gulf Coast ZooMarch 14, 2026ViewRed Wolf Update: A Big Step for Jenkins
If you’ve been following the journey of our two new red wolves, Jenkins and Walker, we have a wonderful milestone to share. Jenkins has been spotted exploring the yard of his habitat during the day.
This is an exciting sign that he’s becoming more comfortable in his surroundings and beginning to confidently investigate his new environment. For a species that is naturally shy and cautious, especially in human care, this kind of daytime exploration is a meaningful step forward. 

Want to learn more about these critically endangered wolves? Come visit the Zoo and see conservation in action.

 DYK?
Red wolves are one of the most critically endangered canids in the world.
A few key facts:
* Fewer than 20 red wolves remain in the wild today, all in eastern North Carolina.
* A little over 200 red wolves live under human care in zoos and wildlife centers.
* The SAFE (Saving Animals From Extinction) American Red Wolf Program works to research, breed, and prepare these wolves for potential release back into the wild.
* Protecting red wolves helps protect entire ecosystems by keeping populations of deer, raccoons, and rodents in balance.Read more21/5Alabama Gulf Coast ZooMarch 14, 2026ViewWe’re out and about at the BB-Q & Blues Cook Off in Downtown Foley!

Come on out and see us — we’ve brought some of our favorite Animal Ambassadors along for the fun!

Say hello to Rose the opossum, Lucy the three‑banded armadillo, Mia the Central American boa, and Mailbox the box turtle. They’re soaking up the sunshine, the music, and all the friendly faces.

If you’re wandering the festival today, swing by and visit. We’d love to see you!

#SupportYourLocalZoo #AnimalsandArt #AGCZArtontheWildSideRead moreAlabama Gulf Coast ZooMarch 14, 2026ViewRed Wolf Update: A Big Step for Jenkins
If you’ve been following the journey of our two new red wolves, Jenkins and Walker, we have a wonderful milestone to share. Jenkins has been spotted exploring the yard of his habitat during the day.
This is an exciting sign that he’s becoming more comfortable in his surroundings and beginning to confidently investigate his new environment. For a species that is naturally shy and cautious, especially in human care, this kind of daytime exploration is a meaningful step forward. 

Want to learn more about these critically endangered wolves? Come visit the Zoo and see conservation in action.

 DYK?
Red wolves are one of the most critically endangered canids in the world.
A few key facts:
* Fewer than 20 red wolves remain in the wild today, all in eastern North Carolina.
* A little over 200 red wolves live under human care in zoos and wildlife centers.
* The SAFE (Saving Animals From Extinction) American Red Wolf Program works to research, breed, and prepare these wolves for potential release back into the wild.
* Protecting red wolves helps protect entire ecosystems by keeping populations of deer, raccoons, and rodents in balance.Read more21/5Alabama Gulf Coast ZooMarch 14, 2026ViewWe’re out and about at the BB-Q & Blues Cook Off in Downtown Foley!

Come on out and see us — we’ve brought some of our favorite Animal Ambassadors along for the fun!

Say hello to Rose the opossum, Lucy the three‑banded armadillo, Mia the Central American boa, and Mailbox the box turtle. They’re soaking up the sunshine, the music, and all the friendly faces.

If you’re wandering the festival today, swing by and visit. We’d love to see you!

review.reviewBody: Nice
Gulf Shores hidden gem.

Really fun time with the family here. Clean inside the buildings and the staff was nice to us. We had a group of 12 😅  Do you guys have a link for purchasing merchandise online? My son retrospectively would like a T-shirt but we&#039;re back home now in TX lol

Kids fed the giraffe! Honestly the only disappointing thing was the cost of the stuffed animals. $25 a piece? I would&#039;ve gotten em but I&#039;m not spending $100 (4 kiddos) on a regular stuffed animal.

I really want half my money back.  Nothing was really open .  Almost all the animals was gone or inside .  No food bar , the best thing was feeding the animals.  This was a waste of time and really doesn’t deserve a rating.  If you are not going to be able to give what you advertise please stop .  Thank you
A bit on the small side for the cost of admission. Imo BUT has lots of small monkeys monkeys and all the cats Displays are well laid out as we could see all the critters
The animals were well cared for. It was a very pretty zoo with lots of very neat animals.

What staff we came across were friendly, most animals were lazy, &amp; didn&#039;t move around, it was a warm day, but still?? Anything extra like walking in the lemuer enclosure was x-tra ( $25 )  prices were way high, not worth the price. So underwhelmed with my experience.
Okay,  very nice,  clean and friendly.  Nice paths to stroll. Could have more benches and more animals. Sad to say but needs more animals.

Perfect size zoo, you can see every exhibit in a morning or afternoon. Great variety of monkeys and cats. But they have a surprising amount of other animals. You can buy tickets to feed the giraffes too.
The worst zoo we went there 6 moths ago and the cashier was just horribly disrespectful. The zoo is too expensive the enclosures were dirty.

#SupportYourLocalZoo #AnimalsandArt #AGCZArtontheWildSideRead moreAlabama Gulf Coast ZooMarch 14, 2026ViewRed Wolf Update: A Big Step for Jenkins
If you’ve been following the journey of our two new red wolves, Jenkins and Walker, we have a wonderful milestone to share. Jenkins has been spotted exploring the yard of his habitat during the day.
This is an exciting sign that he’s becoming more comfortable in his surroundings and beginning to confidently investigate his new environment. For a species that is naturally shy and cautious, especially in human care, this kind of daytime exploration is a meaningful step forward. 

Want to learn more about these critically endangered wolves? Come visit the Zoo and see conservation in action.

 DYK?
Red wolves are one of the most critically endangered canids in the world.
A few key facts:
* Fewer than 20 red wolves remain in the wild today, all in eastern North Carolina.
* A little over 200 red wolves live under human care in zoos and wildlife centers.
* The SAFE (Saving Animals From Extinction) American Red Wolf Program works to research, breed, and prepare these wolves for potential release back into the wild.
* Protecting red wolves helps protect entire ecosystems by keeping populations of deer, raccoons, and rodents in balance.Read more21/5Alabama Gulf Coast ZooMarch 14, 2026ViewWe’re out and about at the BB-Q & Blues Cook Off in Downtown Foley!

Come on out and see us — we’ve brought some of our favorite Animal Ambassadors along for the fun!

Say hello to Rose the opossum, Lucy the three‑banded armadillo, Mia the Central American boa, and Mailbox the box turtle. They’re soaking up the sunshine, the music, and all the friendly faces.

If you’re wandering the festival today, swing by and visit. We’d love to see you!

review.reviewBody: Nice
Gulf Shores hidden gem.

Really fun time with the family here. Clean inside the buildings and the staff was nice to us. We had a group of 12 😅  Do you guys have a link for purchasing merchandise online? My son retrospectively would like a T-shirt but we&#039;re back home now in TX lol

Kids fed the giraffe! Honestly the only disappointing thing was the cost of the stuffed animals. $25 a piece? I would&#039;ve gotten em but I&#039;m not spending $100 (4 kiddos) on a regular stuffed animal.

I really want half my money back.  Nothing was really open .  Almost all the animals was gone or inside .  No food bar , the best thing was feeding the animals.  This was a waste of time and really doesn’t deserve a rating.  If you are not going to be able to give what you advertise please stop .  Thank you
A bit on the small side for the cost of admission. Imo BUT has lots of small monkeys monkeys and all the cats Displays are well laid out as we could see all the critters
The animals were well cared for. It was a very pretty zoo with lots of very neat animals.

What staff we came across were friendly, most animals were lazy, &amp; didn&#039;t move around, it was a warm day, but still?? Anything extra like walking in the lemuer enclosure was x-tra ( $25 )  prices were way high, not worth the price. So underwhelmed with my experience.
Okay,  very nice,  clean and friendly.  Nice paths to stroll. Could have more benches and more animals. Sad to say but needs more animals.

Perfect size zoo, you can see every exhibit in a morning or afternoon. Great variety of monkeys and cats. But they have a surprising amount of other animals. You can buy tickets to feed the giraffes too.
The worst zoo we went there 6 moths ago and the cashier was just horribly disrespectful. The zoo is too expensive the enclosures were dirty.

#SupportYourLocalZoo #AnimalsandArt #AGCZArtontheWildSideRead moreAlabama Gulf Coast ZooMarch 14, 2026ViewRed Wolf Update: A Big Step for Jenkins
If you’ve been following the journey of our two new red wolves, Jenkins and Walker, we have a wonderful milestone to share. Jenkins has been spotted exploring the yard of his habitat during the day.
This is an exciting sign that he’s becoming more comfortable in his surroundings and beginning to confidently investigate his new environment. For a species that is naturally shy and cautious, especially in human care, this kind of daytime exploration is a meaningful step forward. 

Want to learn more about these critically endangered wolves? Come visit the Zoo and see conservation in action.

 DYK?
Red wolves are one of the most critically endangered canids in the world.
A few key facts:
* Fewer than 20 red wolves remain in the wild today, all in eastern North Carolina.
* A little over 200 red wolves live under human care in zoos and wildlife centers.
* The SAFE (Saving Animals From Extinction) American Red Wolf Program works to research, breed, and prepare these wolves for potential release back into the wild.
* Protecting red wolves helps protect entire ecosystems by keeping populations of deer, raccoons, and rodents in balance.Read more21/5Alabama Gulf Coast ZooMarch 14, 2026ViewWe’re out and about at the BB-Q & Blues Cook Off in Downtown Foley!

Say hello to Rose the opossum, Lucy the three‑banded armadillo, Mia the Central American boa, and Mailbox the box turtle. They’re soaking up the sunshine, the music, and all the friendly faces.

If you’re wandering the festival today, swing by and visit. We’d love to see you!

review.reviewBody: Nice
Gulf Shores hidden gem.

Really fun time with the family here. Clean inside the buildings and the staff was nice to us. We had a group of 12 😅  Do you guys have a link for purchasing merchandise online? My son retrospectively would like a T-shirt but we&#039;re back home now in TX lol

Kids fed the giraffe! Honestly the only disappointing thing was the cost of the stuffed animals. $25 a piece? I would&#039;ve gotten em but I&#039;m not spending $100 (4 kiddos) on a regular stuffed animal.

I really want half my money back.  Nothing was really open .  Almost all the animals was gone or inside .  No food bar , the best thing was feeding the animals.  This was a waste of time and really doesn’t deserve a rating.  If you are not going to be able to give what you advertise please stop .  Thank you
A bit on the small side for the cost of admission. Imo BUT has lots of small monkeys monkeys and all the cats Displays are well laid out as we could see all the critters
The animals were well cared for. It was a very pretty zoo with lots of very neat animals.

What staff we came across were friendly, most animals were lazy, &amp; didn&#039;t move around, it was a warm day, but still?? Anything extra like walking in the lemuer enclosure was x-tra ( $25 )  prices were way high, not worth the price. So underwhelmed with my experience.
Okay,  very nice,  clean and friendly.  Nice paths to stroll. Could have more benches and more animals. Sad to say but needs more animals.

Perfect size zoo, you can see every exhibit in a morning or afternoon. Great variety of monkeys and cats. But they have a surprising amount of other animals. You can buy tickets to feed the giraffes too.
The worst zoo we went there 6 moths ago and the cashier was just horribly disrespectful. The zoo is too expensive the enclosures were dirty.

If you’ve been following the journey of our two new red wolves, Jenkins and Walker, we have a wonderful milestone to share. Jenkins has been spotted exploring the yard of his habitat during the day.
This is an exciting sign that he’s becoming more comfortable in his surroundings and beginning to confidently investigate his new environment. For a species that is naturally shy and cautious, especially in human care, this kind of daytime exploration is a meaningful step forward. 

Want to learn more about these critically endangered wolves? Come visit the Zoo and see conservation in action.

 DYK?
Red wolves are one of the most critically endangered canids in the world.
A few key facts:
* Fewer than 20 red wolves remain in the wild today, all in eastern North Carolina.
* A little over 200 red wolves live under human care in zoos and wildlife centers.
* The SAFE (Saving Animals From Extinction) American Red Wolf Program works to research, breed, and prepare these wolves for potential release back into the wild.
* Protecting red wolves helps protect entire ecosystems by keeping populations of deer, raccoons, and rodents in balance.Read more21/5Alabama Gulf Coast ZooMarch 14, 2026ViewWe’re out and about at the BB-Q & Blues Cook Off in Downtown Foley!

Come on out and see us — we’ve brought some of our favorite Animal Ambassadors along for the fun!

Say hello to Rose the opossum, Lucy the three‑banded armadillo, Mia the Central American boa, and Mailbox the box turtle. They’re soaking up the sunshine, the music, and all the friendly faces.

If you’re wandering the festival today, swing by and visit. We’d love to see you!

review.reviewBody: Nice
Gulf Shores hidden gem.

Really fun time with the family here. Clean inside the buildings and the staff was nice to us. We had a group of 12 😅  Do you guys have a link for purchasing merchandise online? My son retrospectively would like a T-shirt but we&#039;re back home now in TX lol

Kids fed the giraffe! Honestly the only disappointing thing was the cost of the stuffed animals. $25 a piece? I would&#039;ve gotten em but I&#039;m not spending $100 (4 kiddos) on a regular stuffed animal.

I really want half my money back.  Nothing was really open .  Almost all the animals was gone or inside .  No food bar , the best thing was feeding the animals.  This was a waste of time and really doesn’t deserve a rating.  If you are not going to be able to give what you advertise please stop .  Thank you
A bit on the small side for the cost of admission. Imo BUT has lots of small monkeys monkeys and all the cats Displays are well laid out as we could see all the critters
The animals were well cared for. It was a very pretty zoo with lots of very neat animals.

What staff we came across were friendly, most animals were lazy, &amp; didn&#039;t move around, it was a warm day, but still?? Anything extra like walking in the lemuer enclosure was x-tra ( $25 )  prices were way high, not worth the price. So underwhelmed with my experience.
Okay,  very nice,  clean and friendly.  Nice paths to stroll. Could have more benches and more animals. Sad to say but needs more animals.

Perfect size zoo, you can see every exhibit in a morning or afternoon. Great variety of monkeys and cats. But they have a surprising amount of other animals. You can buy tickets to feed the giraffes too.
The worst zoo we went there 6 moths ago and the cashier was just horribly disrespectful. The zoo is too expensive the enclosures were dirty.

review.reviewBody: Nice
Gulf Shores hidden gem.

Really fun time with the family here. Clean inside the buildings and the staff was nice to us. We had a group of 12 😅  Do you guys have a link for purchasing merchandise online? My son retrospectively would like a T-shirt but we&#039;re back home now in TX lol

Kids fed the giraffe! Honestly the only disappointing thing was the cost of the stuffed animals. $25 a piece? I would&#039;ve gotten em but I&#039;m not spending $100 (4 kiddos) on a regular stuffed animal.

I really want half my money back.  Nothing was really open .  Almost all the animals was gone or inside .  No food bar , the best thing was feeding the animals.  This was a waste of time and really doesn’t deserve a rating.  If you are not going to be able to give what you advertise please stop .  Thank you
A bit on the small side for the cost of admission. Imo BUT has lots of small monkeys monkeys and all the cats Displays are well laid out as we could see all the critters
The animals were well cared for. It was a very pretty zoo with lots of very neat animals.

What staff we came across were friendly, most animals were lazy, &amp; didn&#039;t move around, it was a warm day, but still?? Anything extra like walking in the lemuer enclosure was x-tra ( $25 )  prices were way high, not worth the price. So underwhelmed with my experience.
Okay,  very nice,  clean and friendly.  Nice paths to stroll. Could have more benches and more animals. Sad to say but needs more animals.

Perfect size zoo, you can see every exhibit in a morning or afternoon. Great variety of monkeys and cats. But they have a surprising amount of other animals. You can buy tickets to feed the giraffes too.
The worst zoo we went there 6 moths ago and the cashier was just horribly disrespectful. The zoo is too expensive the enclosures were dirty.

#SupportYourLocalZoo #AnimalsandArt #AGCZArtontheWildSideRead moreAlabama Gulf Coast ZooMarch 14, 2026ViewRed Wolf Update: A Big Step for Jenkins
If you’ve been following the journey of our two new red wolves, Jenkins and Walker, we have a wonderful milestone to share. Jenkins has been spotted exploring the yard of his habitat during the day.
This is an exciting sign that he’s becoming more comfortable in his surroundings and beginning to confidently investigate his new environment. For a species that is naturally shy and cautious, especially in human care, this kind of daytime exploration is a meaningful step forward. 

Want to learn more about these critically endangered wolves? Come visit the Zoo and see conservation in action.

 DYK?
Red wolves are one of the most critically endangered canids in the world.
A few key facts:
* Fewer than 20 red wolves remain in the wild today, all in eastern North Carolina.
* A little over 200 red wolves live under human care in zoos and wildlife centers.
* The SAFE (Saving Animals From Extinction) American Red Wolf Program works to research, breed, and prepare these wolves for potential release back into the wild.
* Protecting red wolves helps protect entire ecosystems by keeping populations of deer, raccoons, and rodents in balance.Read more21/5Alabama Gulf Coast ZooMarch 14, 2026ViewWe’re out and about at the BB-Q & Blues Cook Off in Downtown Foley!

Come on out and see us — we’ve brought some of our favorite Animal Ambassadors along for the fun!

Say hello to Rose the opossum, Lucy the three‑banded armadillo, Mia the Central American boa, and Mailbox the box turtle. They’re soaking up the sunshine, the music, and all the friendly faces.

If you’re wandering the festival today, swing by and visit. We’d love to see you!

#SupportYourLocalZoo #AnimalsandArt #AGCZArtontheWildSideRead moreAlabama Gulf Coast ZooMarch 14, 2026ViewRed Wolf Update: A Big Step for Jenkins
If you’ve been following the journey of our two new red wolves, Jenkins and Walker, we have a wonderful milestone to share. Jenkins has been spotted exploring the yard of his habitat during the day.
This is an exciting sign that he’s becoming more comfortable in his surroundings and beginning to confidently investigate his new environment. For a species that is naturally shy and cautious, especially in human care, this kind of daytime exploration is a meaningful step forward. 

Want to learn more about these critically endangered wolves? Come visit the Zoo and see conservation in action.

 DYK?
Red wolves are one of the most critically endangered canids in the world.
A few key facts:
* Fewer than 20 red wolves remain in the wild today, all in eastern North Carolina.
* A little over 200 red wolves live under human care in zoos and wildlife centers.
* The SAFE (Saving Animals From Extinction) American Red Wolf Program works to research, breed, and prepare these wolves for potential release back into the wild.
* Protecting red wolves helps protect entire ecosystems by keeping populations of deer, raccoons, and rodents in balance.Read more21/5Alabama Gulf Coast ZooMarch 14, 2026ViewWe’re out and about at the BB-Q & Blues Cook Off in Downtown Foley!

Come on out and see us — we’ve brought some of our favorite Animal Ambassadors along for the fun!

Say hello to Rose the opossum, Lucy the three‑banded armadillo, Mia the Central American boa, and Mailbox the box turtle. They’re soaking up the sunshine, the music, and all the friendly faces.

If you’re wandering the festival today, swing by and visit. We’d love to see you!

review.reviewBody: Nice
Gulf Shores hidden gem.

Really fun time with the family here. Clean inside the buildings and the staff was nice to us. We had a group of 12 😅  Do you guys have a link for purchasing merchandise online? My son retrospectively would like a T-shirt but we&#039;re back home now in TX lol

Kids fed the giraffe! Honestly the only disappointing thing was the cost of the stuffed animals. $25 a piece? I would&#039;ve gotten em but I&#039;m not spending $100 (4 kiddos) on a regular stuffed animal.

I really want half my money back.  Nothing was really open .  Almost all the animals was gone or inside .  No food bar , the best thing was feeding the animals.  This was a waste of time and really doesn’t deserve a rating.  If you are not going to be able to give what you advertise please stop .  Thank you
A bit on the small side for the cost of admission. Imo BUT has lots of small monkeys monkeys and all the cats Displays are well laid out as we could see all the critters
The animals were well cared for. It was a very pretty zoo with lots of very neat animals.

What staff we came across were friendly, most animals were lazy, &amp; didn&#039;t move around, it was a warm day, but still?? Anything extra like walking in the lemuer enclosure was x-tra ( $25 )  prices were way high, not worth the price. So underwhelmed with my experience.
Okay,  very nice,  clean and friendly.  Nice paths to stroll. Could have more benches and more animals. Sad to say but needs more animals.

Perfect size zoo, you can see every exhibit in a morning or afternoon. Great variety of monkeys and cats. But they have a surprising amount of other animals. You can buy tickets to feed the giraffes too.
The worst zoo we went there 6 moths ago and the cashier was just horribly disrespectful. The zoo is too expensive the enclosures were dirty.

#SupportYourLocalZoo #AnimalsandArt #AGCZArtontheWildSideRead moreAlabama Gulf Coast ZooMarch 14, 2026ViewRed Wolf Update: A Big Step for Jenkins
If you’ve been following the journey of our two new red wolves, Jenkins and Walker, we have a wonderful milestone to share. Jenkins has been spotted exploring the yard of his habitat during the day.
This is an exciting sign that he’s becoming more comfortable in his surroundings and beginning to confidently investigate his new environment. For a species that is naturally shy and cautious, especially in human care, this kind of daytime exploration is a meaningful step forward. 

Want to learn more about these critically endangered wolves? Come visit the Zoo and see conservation in action.

 DYK?
Red wolves are one of the most critically endangered canids in the world.
A few key facts:
* Fewer than 20 red wolves remain in the wild today, all in eastern North Carolina.
* A little over 200 red wolves live under human care in zoos and wildlife centers.
* The SAFE (Saving Animals From Extinction) American Red Wolf Program works to research, breed, and prepare these wolves for potential release back into the wild.
* Protecting red wolves helps protect entire ecosystems by keeping populations of deer, raccoons, and rodents in balance.Read more21/5Alabama Gulf Coast ZooMarch 14, 2026ViewWe’re out and about at the BB-Q & Blues Cook Off in Downtown Foley!

Say hello to Rose the opossum, Lucy the three‑banded armadillo, Mia the Central American boa, and Mailbox the box turtle. They’re soaking up the sunshine, the music, and all the friendly faces.

If you’re wandering the festival today, swing by and visit. We’d love to see you!

review.reviewBody: Nice
Gulf Shores hidden gem.

Really fun time with the family here. Clean inside the buildings and the staff was nice to us. We had a group of 12 😅  Do you guys have a link for purchasing merchandise online? My son retrospectively would like a T-shirt but we&#039;re back home now in TX lol

Kids fed the giraffe! Honestly the only disappointing thing was the cost of the stuffed animals. $25 a piece? I would&#039;ve gotten em but I&#039;m not spending $100 (4 kiddos) on a regular stuffed animal.

I really want half my money back.  Nothing was really open .  Almost all the animals was gone or inside .  No food bar , the best thing was feeding the animals.  This was a waste of time and really doesn’t deserve a rating.  If you are not going to be able to give what you advertise please stop .  Thank you
A bit on the small side for the cost of admission. Imo BUT has lots of small monkeys monkeys and all the cats Displays are well laid out as we could see all the critters
The animals were well cared for. It was a very pretty zoo with lots of very neat animals.

What staff we came across were friendly, most animals were lazy, &amp; didn&#039;t move around, it was a warm day, but still?? Anything extra like walking in the lemuer enclosure was x-tra ( $25 )  prices were way high, not worth the price. So underwhelmed with my experience.
Okay,  very nice,  clean and friendly.  Nice paths to stroll. Could have more benches and more animals. Sad to say but needs more animals.

Perfect size zoo, you can see every exhibit in a morning or afternoon. Great variety of monkeys and cats. But they have a surprising amount of other animals. You can buy tickets to feed the giraffes too.
The worst zoo we went there 6 moths ago and the cashier was just horribly disrespectful. The zoo is too expensive the enclosures were dirty.

If you’ve been following the journey of our two new red wolves, Jenkins and Walker, we have a wonderful milestone to share. Jenkins has been spotted exploring the yard of his habitat during the day.
This is an exciting sign that he’s becoming more comfortable in his surroundings and beginning to confidently investigate his new environment. For a species that is naturally shy and cautious, especially in human care, this kind of daytime exploration is a meaningful step forward. 

Want to learn more about these critically endangered wolves? Come visit the Zoo and see conservation in action.

 DYK?
Red wolves are one of the most critically endangered canids in the world.
A few key facts:
* Fewer than 20 red wolves remain in the wild today, all in eastern North Carolina.
* A little over 200 red wolves live under human care in zoos and wildlife centers.
* The SAFE (Saving Animals From Extinction) American Red Wolf Program works to research, breed, and prepare these wolves for potential release back into the wild.
* Protecting red wolves helps protect entire ecosystems by keeping populations of deer, raccoons, and rodents in balance.Read more21/5Alabama Gulf Coast ZooMarch 14, 2026ViewWe’re out and about at the BB-Q & Blues Cook Off in Downtown Foley!

Come on out and see us — we’ve brought some of our favorite Animal Ambassadors along for the fun!

Say hello to Rose the opossum, Lucy the three‑banded armadillo, Mia the Central American boa, and Mailbox the box turtle. They’re soaking up the sunshine, the music, and all the friendly faces.

If you’re wandering the festival today, swing by and visit. We’d love to see you!

review.reviewBody: Nice
Gulf Shores hidden gem.

Really fun time with the family here. Clean inside the buildings and the staff was nice to us. We had a group of 12 😅  Do you guys have a link for purchasing merchandise online? My son retrospectively would like a T-shirt but we&#039;re back home now in TX lol

Kids fed the giraffe! Honestly the only disappointing thing was the cost of the stuffed animals. $25 a piece? I would&#039;ve gotten em but I&#039;m not spending $100 (4 kiddos) on a regular stuffed animal.

I really want half my money back.  Nothing was really open .  Almost all the animals was gone or inside .  No food bar , the best thing was feeding the animals.  This was a waste of time and really doesn’t deserve a rating.  If you are not going to be able to give what you advertise please stop .  Thank you
A bit on the small side for the cost of admission. Imo BUT has lots of small monkeys monkeys and all the cats Displays are well laid out as we could see all the critters
The animals were well cared for. It was a very pretty zoo with lots of very neat animals.

What staff we came across were friendly, most animals were lazy, &amp; didn&#039;t move around, it was a warm day, but still?? Anything extra like walking in the lemuer enclosure was x-tra ( $25 )  prices were way high, not worth the price. So underwhelmed with my experience.
Okay,  very nice,  clean and friendly.  Nice paths to stroll. Could have more benches and more animals. Sad to say but needs more animals.

Perfect size zoo, you can see every exhibit in a morning or afternoon. Great variety of monkeys and cats. But they have a surprising amount of other animals. You can buy tickets to feed the giraffes too.
The worst zoo we went there 6 moths ago and the cashier was just horribly disrespectful. The zoo is too expensive the enclosures were dirty.

#SupportYourLocalZoo #AnimalsandArt #AGCZArtontheWildSideRead moreAlabama Gulf Coast ZooMarch 14, 2026ViewRed Wolf Update: A Big Step for Jenkins
If you’ve been following the journey of our two new red wolves, Jenkins and Walker, we have a wonderful milestone to share. Jenkins has been spotted exploring the yard of his habitat during the day.
This is an exciting sign that he’s becoming more comfortable in his surroundings and beginning to confidently investigate his new environment. For a species that is naturally shy and cautious, especially in human care, this kind of daytime exploration is a meaningful step forward. 

Want to learn more about these critically endangered wolves? Come visit the Zoo and see conservation in action.

 DYK?
Red wolves are one of the most critically endangered canids in the world.
A few key facts:
* Fewer than 20 red wolves remain in the wild today, all in eastern North Carolina.
* A little over 200 red wolves live under human care in zoos and wildlife centers.
* The SAFE (Saving Animals From Extinction) American Red Wolf Program works to research, breed, and prepare these wolves for potential release back into the wild.
* Protecting red wolves helps protect entire ecosystems by keeping populations of deer, raccoons, and rodents in balance.Read more21/5Alabama Gulf Coast ZooMarch 14, 2026ViewWe’re out and about at the BB-Q & Blues Cook Off in Downtown Foley!

Come on out and see us — we’ve brought some of our favorite Animal Ambassadors along for the fun!

Say hello to Rose the opossum, Lucy the three‑banded armadillo, Mia the Central American boa, and Mailbox the box turtle. They’re soaking up the sunshine, the music, and all the friendly faces.

If you’re wandering the festival today, swing by and visit. We’d love to see you!

review.reviewBody: Nice
Gulf Shores hidden gem.

Really fun time with the family here. Clean inside the buildings and the staff was nice to us. We had a group of 12 😅  Do you guys have a link for purchasing merchandise online? My son retrospectively would like a T-shirt but we&#039;re back home now in TX lol

Kids fed the giraffe! Honestly the only disappointing thing was the cost of the stuffed animals. $25 a piece? I would&#039;ve gotten em but I&#039;m not spending $100 (4 kiddos) on a regular stuffed animal.

I really want half my money back.  Nothing was really open .  Almost all the animals was gone or inside .  No food bar , the best thing was feeding the animals.  This was a waste of time and really doesn’t deserve a rating.  If you are not going to be able to give what you advertise please stop .  Thank you
A bit on the small side for the cost of admission. Imo BUT has lots of small monkeys monkeys and all the cats Displays are well laid out as we could see all the critters
The animals were well cared for. It was a very pretty zoo with lots of very neat animals.

What staff we came across were friendly, most animals were lazy, &amp; didn&#039;t move around, it was a warm day, but still?? Anything extra like walking in the lemuer enclosure was x-tra ( $25 )  prices were way high, not worth the price. So underwhelmed with my experience.
Okay,  very nice,  clean and friendly.  Nice paths to stroll. Could have more benches and more animals. Sad to say but needs more animals.

Perfect size zoo, you can see every exhibit in a morning or afternoon. Great variety of monkeys and cats. But they have a surprising amount of other animals. You can buy tickets to feed the giraffes too.
The worst zoo we went there 6 moths ago and the cashier was just horribly disrespectful. The zoo is too expensive the enclosures were dirty.

If you’ve been following the journey of our two new red wolves, Jenkins and Walker, we have a wonderful milestone to share. Jenkins has been spotted exploring the yard of his habitat during the day.
This is an exciting sign that he’s becoming more comfortable in his surroundings and beginning to confidently investigate his new environment. For a species that is naturally shy and cautious, especially in human care, this kind of daytime exploration is a meaningful step forward. 

Want to learn more about these critically endangered wolves? Come visit the Zoo and see conservation in action.

 DYK?
Red wolves are one of the most critically endangered canids in the world.
A few key facts:
* Fewer than 20 red wolves remain in the wild today, all in eastern North Carolina.
* A little over 200 red wolves live under human care in zoos and wildlife centers.
* The SAFE (Saving Animals From Extinction) American Red Wolf Program works to research, breed, and prepare these wolves for potential release back into the wild.

review.reviewBody: Nice
Gulf Shores hidden gem.

Really fun time with the family here. Clean inside the buildings and the staff was nice to us. We had a group of 12 😅  Do you guys have a link for purchasing merchandise online? My son retrospectively would like a T-shirt but we&#039;re back home now in TX lol

Kids fed the giraffe! Honestly the only disappointing thing was the cost of the stuffed animals. $25 a piece? I would&#039;ve gotten em but I&#039;m not spending $100 (4 kiddos) on a regular stuffed animal.

I really want half my money back.  Nothing was really open .  Almost all the animals was gone or inside .  No food bar , the best thing was feeding the animals.  This was a waste of time and really doesn’t deserve a rating.  If you are not going to be able to give what you advertise please stop .  Thank you
A bit on the small side for the cost of admission. Imo BUT has lots of small monkeys monkeys and all the cats Displays are well laid out as we could see all the critters
The animals were well cared for. It was a very pretty zoo with lots of very neat animals.

What staff we came across were friendly, most animals were lazy, &amp; didn&#039;t move around, it was a warm day, but still?? Anything extra like walking in the lemuer enclosure was x-tra ( $25 )  prices were way high, not worth the price. So underwhelmed with my experience.
Okay,  very nice,  clean and friendly.  Nice paths to stroll. Could have more benches and more animals. Sad to say but needs more animals.

Perfect size zoo, you can see every exhibit in a morning or afternoon. Great variety of monkeys and cats. But they have a surprising amount of other animals. You can buy tickets to feed the giraffes too.
The worst zoo we went there 6 moths ago and the cashier was just horribly disrespectful. The zoo is too expensive the enclosures were dirty.

If you’ve been following the journey of our two new red wolves, Jenkins and Walker, we have a wonderful milestone to share. Jenkins has been spotted exploring the yard of his habitat during the day.
This is an exciting sign that he’s becoming more comfortable in his surroundings and beginning to confidently investigate his new environment. For a species that is naturally shy and cautious, especially in human care, this kind of daytime exploration is a meaningful step forward. 

Want to learn more about these critically endangered wolves? Come visit the Zoo and see conservation in action.

 DYK?
Red wolves are one of the most critically endangered canids in the world.
A few key facts:
* Fewer than 20 red wolves remain in the wild today, all in eastern North Carolina.
* A little over 200 red wolves live under human care in zoos and wildlife centers.
* The SAFE (Saving Animals From Extinction) American Red Wolf Program works to research, breed, and prepare these wolves for potential release back into the wild.
* Protecting red wolves helps protect entire ecosystems by keeping populations of deer, raccoons, and rodents in balance.Read more21/5Alabama Gulf Coast ZooMarch 14, 2026ViewWe’re out and about at the BB-Q & Blues Cook Off in Downtown Foley!

Come on out and see us — we’ve brought some of our favorite Animal Ambassadors along for the fun!

Say hello to Rose the opossum, Lucy the three‑banded armadillo, Mia the Central American boa, and Mailbox the box turtle. They’re soaking up the sunshine, the music, and all the friendly faces.

If you’re wandering the festival today, swing by and visit. We’d love to see you!

review.reviewBody: Nice
Gulf Shores hidden gem.

Really fun time with the family here. Clean inside the buildings and the staff was nice to us. We had a group of 12 😅  Do you guys have a link for purchasing merchandise online? My son retrospectively would like a T-shirt but we&#039;re back home now in TX lol

Kids fed the giraffe! Honestly the only disappointing thing was the cost of the stuffed animals. $25 a piece? I would&#039;ve gotten em but I&#039;m not spending $100 (4 kiddos) on a regular stuffed animal.

I really want half my money back.  Nothing was really open .  Almost all the animals was gone or inside .  No food bar , the best thing was feeding the animals.  This was a waste of time and really doesn’t deserve a rating.  If you are not going to be able to give what you advertise please stop .  Thank you
A bit on the small side for the cost of admission. Imo BUT has lots of small monkeys monkeys and all the cats Displays are well laid out as we could see all the critters
The animals were well cared for. It was a very pretty zoo with lots of very neat animals.

What staff we came across were friendly, most animals were lazy, &amp; didn&#039;t move around, it was a warm day, but still?? Anything extra like walking in the lemuer enclosure was x-tra ( $25 )  prices were way high, not worth the price. So underwhelmed with my experience.
Okay,  very nice,  clean and friendly.  Nice paths to stroll. Could have more benches and more animals. Sad to say but needs more animals.

Perfect size zoo, you can see every exhibit in a morning or afternoon. Great variety of monkeys and cats. But they have a surprising amount of other animals. You can buy tickets to feed the giraffes too.
The worst zoo we went there 6 moths ago and the cashier was just horribly disrespectful. The zoo is too expensive the enclosures were dirty.

 About The Zoo 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Mission Statement 
 
 The mission of the Alabama Gulf Coast Zoo is to create compelling experiences that connect people and community with wildlife, and inspire personal responsibility for conservation of the natural world. Education. Conservation. Adventure. Community. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 About The Zoo 
 
 The zoo is about 6 miles from the beach. Tucked just off the main highway, visitors feel like they have entered a tropical urban oasis filled with intriguing sounds from our rich diversity of exotic animals. Whether it’s the distinctive call from our peacocks or chatter from our monkeys you are instantly transported out of life’s hustle and bustle into our peaceful kingdom.Voted the “#1 Zoo in Alabama” for two years running!If you really want something extra unforgettable, stop in for a one-on-one, up-close experience with a few of our friendliest friends at our Animal Encounters! 
 
 
 
 Explore Our Full History!

 Teresa Wilkerson 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 The Alabama Gulf Coast Zoo is operated by The Zoo Foundation, Inc., a non-profit 501(c)(3) organization, governed by a Board of Directors. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Safety First 
 
 The safety of every zoo visitor, our staff, and our animals have precedence over everything at the Alabama Gulf Coast Zoo. We follow every safety protocol as required by law, and receive 100% compliance by the United States Department of Agriculture (USDA), the federal agency that annually inspects our facility. We maintain ongoing safety training procedures in the handling of our animals by our keepers, and stay vigilant in keeping our facility structures secure. We take great pride in our constant efforts to provide the safest and most secure environment we can for your family when you come to visit ours. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Sources of Revenue 
 
 As a non-profit 501(c)(3) organization, the Alabama Gulf Coast Zoo relies solely on admissions, memberships, and contributions to remain in business.  
 
 Construction of the new Alabama Gulf Coast Zoo is an on going project and our Philanthropy Partnership Program plays an extremely significant role.It ensures that the zoo becomes a prominent member of an ever-growing business and civic community in its new Gulf Shores location, while offering education, entertainment, and cultural activities, especially for families.By participating in one of the zoo’s many partnership programs, you, your company, organization, or institution can contribute to the zoo’s vibrant, secure standing far into the future. 
 
 For more about the Alabama Gulf Coast ZooPhilanthropy Partnership Program,CONTACT:Director of Development – Paula White251.256.7008 | development@algulfcoastzoo.orgThe Alabama Gulf Coast Zoo is operated by The Zoo Foundation Inc., a 501(c)(3) non-profit organization governed by a board of directors. Your donation is tax-deductible to the full extent permitted by law. Please consult with your tax advisor.

 One of the most meaningful and visible ways to support the Alabama Gulf Coast Zoo is to become an animal or exhibit sponsor. Each of our current exhibits can be sponsored to provide care and feeding for that animal for the year. Additional sponsorships are available to help us expand and grow with new exhibits.

If you’ve been following the journey of our two new red wolves, Jenkins and Walker, we have a wonderful milestone to share. Jenkins has been spotted exploring the yard of his habitat during the day.

Want to learn more about these critically endangered wolves? Come visit the Zoo and see conservation in action.

 DYK?
Red wolves are one of the most critically endangered canids in the world.
A few key facts:
* Fewer than 20 red wolves remain in the wild today, all in eastern North Carolina.
* A little over 200 red wolves live under human care in zoos and wildlife centers.
* The SAFE (Saving Animals From Extinction) American Red Wolf Program works to research, breed, and prepare these wolves for potential release back into the wild.
